sense: stop someone to talk to them

terms.gloss: buttonhole, take hold of someone to talk to him
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: to take hold of a person in order to talk with him, thank him or entreat him; also to canvass for an office.

phrases.english: I buttonhole my friends, I plead, I go round their houses

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 94, 285.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
